recent_posts.title: Spatial computing will move digital content off screens and into physical space
recent_posts.summary: Spatial computing is presented as an emerging paradigm where digital content escapes flat screens and integrates into physical space. By 2026, devices like AR glasses could overlay information onto the real world, turning floors into interactive surfaces and air into keyboards. The shift is framed as moving from 'looking at' screens to 'being with' digital content, enabling new ways to interact with information and environments.

recent_posts.title: Open Models Coding Essentials – Running LLMs Locally and in the Cloud Course
recent_posts.summary: A hands-on course exploring how to run open-source LLMs (Gemma 4, Kimi, GLM, Qwen, MiniMax) locally and in the cloud for use as coding assistants. The instructor walks through setting up Ollama on Windows/WSL with an RTX 4060, discovering hardware limitations (8GB VRAM is insufficient for 32K context windows needed by Claude Code), and evaluating multiple coding harnesses including Claude Code, Codex, Goose CLI, Kilo, and Pi Coding Agent. Key findings: Kimi 2.5 performed best among open models for agentic coding tasks, Claude Code worked surprisingly well with open models via Ollama Cloud, and most consumer hardware cannot run these models locally at the context sizes required. Ollama Cloud ($20-30/month subscription) is recommended as the most practical cloud serving option.

recent_posts.title: QuRT: The Real-Time OS Inside Your Phone's Processor [Full Handbook]
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive handbook on QuRT (Qualcomm Real-Time Operating System), the RTOS running on Qualcomm's Hexagon DSP inside Snapdragon-powered devices. Covers the full development workflow including SDK setup, SCons build system, thread creation internals (TCB layout, stack frame initialization, context switching), synchronization primitives (mutexes with priority inheritance, condition variables, signals, barriers, semaphores), memory management (TCM vs DDR, cache coherency for shared memory, memory pools for O(1) allocation), hardware-backed timers for periodic DSP workloads, and interrupt handling via QuRT's thread-based ISR model. Includes working C code examples throughout, from a basic hello-world thread to a producer-consumer pipeline and sensor fusion patterns.

recent_posts.title: The full infrastructure stack that powers remote work
recent_posts.summary: Remote work relies on far more than a Wi-Fi connection. It depends on a layered infrastructure stack including cloud platforms, identity and authentication systems, VPNs or zero-trust access models, latency-sensitive networking, and physical hardware. Key concepts covered include why latency matters more than raw bandwidth, how identity has replaced location as the security perimeter, the bottlenecks introduced by traditional VPNs, the value of redundant connectivity options like eSIMs, and how distributed collaboration tools are affected by network reliability. Building a resilient remote setup means planning for failure across all these layers, not just optimizing for convenience.

recent_posts.title: ITCM vs DTCM vs DDR: Embedded Memory Types Explained [Full Handbook]
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive handbook explaining the three main memory types in ARM Cortex-M/R embedded systems: ITCM (Instruction Tightly-Coupled Memory), DTCM (Data Tightly-Coupled Memory), and DDR (Double Data Rate). Covers the fundamental tradeoff between TCM's single-cycle deterministic access and DDR's larger but slower multi-cycle access. Explains what code and data belongs in each region, how to use GCC section attributes and linker scripts to control placement, common pitfalls (stack overflow in DTCM, DMA bus matrix incompatibilities, alignment faults), and multiple methods for profiling memory usage including linker map files, a Python parsing script, the size command, and runtime stack watermarking.

recent_posts.title: AI Paper Review: Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training (GPT-1)
recent_posts.summary: A beginner-friendly review of the original GPT-1 paper ('Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training' by Radford et al., 2018). Covers the paper's core contribution: a two-stage approach of unsupervised pre-training on large text corpora followed by supervised fine-tuning on specific tasks. Explains the Transformer decoder-only architecture used, compares GPT with BERT and the original Transformer, summarizes key results (outperforming state-of-the-art on 9 of 12 tasks), and discusses limitations. Frames GPT-1 as the foundational shift from task-specific models to general-purpose language understanding that led to GPT-2, GPT-3, and ChatGPT.

recent_posts.title: How to Build a Market Research Copilot with MCP and Python [Full Handbook]
recent_posts.summary: A step-by-step guide to building a financial research copilot that tests natural-language investment theses against real market data. The system uses EODHD's MCP server to fetch historical prices and fundamentals, computes price and business-quality signals in Python, classifies the thesis into claim types, builds structured evidence buckets (supporting, contradicting, missing), assigns a verdict, and generates a research memo. The project is split into a thin MCP client layer and a core thesis-testing pipeline, with sanity checks in Jupyter.

recent_posts.title: CodePen 2.0 is now in public beta with a unified extensible editor
recent_posts.summary: CodePen co-founder Chris Coyier announces CodePen 2.0, now in public beta. The redesigned platform unifies multiple editors into one flexible system that retains the classic three-box layout while adding support for multiple files, various preprocessors like Svelte, and an extensible architecture designed to accommodate future processors and tools. The rebuild prioritized backwards compatibility with all existing pens while future-proofing the platform.

recent_posts.title: How to Build a Scoped Note-Taking API with Django Rest Framework and SimpleJWT
recent_posts.summary: A step-by-step guide to building a JWT-authenticated note-taking REST API with Django REST Framework and SimpleJWT. Covers setting up a custom user model, configuring access and refresh tokens, writing serializers that protect sensitive fields (write-only passwords, read-only ownership), and implementing scoped views so each user can only access their own notes. Also explains how to prevent ID enumeration attacks using 404 responses and how to handle token expiration with refresh tokens. Tested end-to-end with Postman.

recent_posts.title: The Complete SOC 2 Type II Implementation Handbook for Engineers: A Month-by-Month Roadmap with Real Commands
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive 90-day engineering roadmap for achieving SOC 2 Type II compliance. Covers scoping the audit boundary with network segmentation, implementing 14 critical controls (MFA, CloudTrail, GuardDuty, VPC Flow Logs, Secrets Manager, EBS encryption, S3 Block Public Access, branch protection, container scanning, incident response, access reviews, backup verification, and change management), building automated evidence collection infrastructure using AWS Lambda and GitHub Actions, selecting an auditor, running a readiness assessment, and managing the observation period. Includes real Terraform, AWS CLI, and Python code for each control.

top_posts.title: How to Deploy a Web App
top_posts.summary: Deploying a web application can be simplified with the right guidance. Kerollos Magdy, a Microsoft software engineer, presents a comprehensive course on the freeCodeCamp.org YouTube channel. The course covers deploying web applications using services like Azure, Render, and MongoDB Atlas. It provides step-by-step instructions, starting with free options and then delving into Azure. It also includes setting up databases, deploying backend services, and integrating frontends, offering a broad understanding of various deployment environments.

top_posts.title: Essential React.js Practices for Optimized Development
top_posts.summary: This guide offers crucial tips on optimizing React development using hooks. It covers the importance of maintaining immutability in state management, avoiding the overuse of useState, leveraging useMemo for performance improvements, ensuring unique keys for list items, and properly handling dependencies in useEffect. The guide also advises on alternatives to useEffect for managing side effects efficiently, contributing to cleaner and more efficient code.

top_posts.title: Master React by Building 25 Projects
top_posts.summary: Learn React and build 25 projects to enhance your understanding of React's capabilities. Course covers various projects including accordion, random color generator, star rating, image slider, and more. Watch the full course on the freeCodeCamp.org YouTube channel.

top_posts.title: 8 React Projects to Build in 2023
top_posts.summary: 8 React Projects to Build in 2023 will show you what's possible to make with React. Check out the React Bootcamp to see how to make each of them step-by-step. Todo apps are a great project to begin with because you don't need any third-party libraries to build them.

top_posts.title: Harvard CS50 2026 – Free Computer Science University Course
top_posts.summary: Harvard's CS50 2026 course is now available as a free 25-hour video series covering fundamental computer science concepts. The course teaches algorithmic thinking and problem-solving through multiple programming languages including C, Python, SQL, HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Topics span algorithms, data structures, memory management, web programming, and a new section on artificial intelligence's impact on computer science. Taught by David J. Malan, the course is designed for beginners with no prior programming experience.
